chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

Jumuʿah becomes obligatory upon seven persons from among the Muslims, and it is not obligatory upon fewer than them: the Imam, his judge, the one claiming a right, the one against whom the claim is made, the two witnesses, and the one who carries out the prescribed penalties before the Imam.

key_terms.الشَّاهِدَانِ: the two witnesses required in the proceeding
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the Imam, the leader presiding over authority
key_terms.الْمُدَّعَى عَلَيْهِ: the defendant, the one against whom the claim is made
key_terms.الْمُدَّعِي: the claimant, the one asserting a right
key_terms.سَبْعَةِ: seven, the minimum number specified here
key_terms.قَاضِيهِ: his judge, the judicial officer associated with the Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum number required for Jumuʿah to be obligatory according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the minimum number upon whom Jumuʿah is obligatory, identifying seven specific individuals. It presents the ruling in a judicial and governing context, linking the obligation of Friday prayer to the presence of core participants in public authority and adjudication.
